page: Microsoft Azure D192lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dldsv7 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs mapped to 96 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor cores running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-CPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It is equipped with 11339 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not include any GPU accelerators. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the D192lds_v7 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 202,853.75 and a PassMark CPU score of 152,145.2. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read bandwidth of 15,083.08 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 688.55 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the average tier. The server excels in data processing tasks, delivering top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (1,146.71 GB/sec) and static web serving throughput (157.94 GB/sec). For database workloads, it achieves top-tier performance with 268.62 million Redis SET operations per second and high PassMark database operations scores.

The primary design tradeoff of the D192lds_v7 is its low memory density relative to its massive compute capacity. While highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints, it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale in-memory analytics. The inclusion of 11,339 GB of local storage provides high-capacity, low-latency local data access, making it highly efficient for local scratch space and high-throughput file processing. Although it lacks dedicated GPU hardware, the CPU's AMX and AVX-512 extensions enable strong performance in CPU-based machine learning tasks, such as prompt processing for 7B and 70B parameter LLMs. Recommended workloads include high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded data compression, CPU-bound batch processing, and database operations with moderate memory requirements.
